seo.title: Snowflake client for {devices}
seo.description: Sign in to Snowflake with a key pair, browser SSO, OAuth or a password and passcode, switch warehouse and role without reconnecting, and unload to a stage.

header.title: Snowflake client
header.lead: Query and edit Snowflake tables, switch warehouses and roles without reconnecting, and export straight to a stage.

bands.title: Connect and sign in
text: Enter the account identifier before .snowflakecomputing.com, such as myorg-myaccount. Requests use HTTPS, so there is no host, TLS section or SSH pane. Snowflake has no URL scheme: name a section in CLI Connection Name, and every field you leave empty is read from ~/.snowflake/connections.toml.

Choose an <ui>Auth Method</ui>: PKCS#8 key pair, browser SSO, OAuth token, or password with <ui>MFA Passcode (TOTP)</ui>. Key pairs need an accurate device clock, and pasted OAuth tokens are not refreshed.

With ALLOW_CLIENT_MFA_CACHING on the account, one fresh passcode is enough: TablePro keeps the MFA token Snowflake returns in the Keychain. With ALLOW_ID_TOKEN, browser SSO keeps a sign-in token there, and later connects skip the browser until Snowflake rejects it.

bands.title: Warehouses, roles and queries
text: Change warehouses and roles with Database > Session Context. The connection keeps one session while idle, and tabs on another database run USE DATABASE before their statements. Object lists come from SHOW commands, which need no warehouse; column details come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA, which does. Explain returns Snowflake’s plan as raw text.

Grid edits bind their values on the server, with VARIANT, OBJECT and ARRAY cells sent through PARSE_JSON. An edit keys on the declared primary key, or on every column when there is none. Standard tables do not enforce key constraints, so an edit or delete reaches every row that shares a duplicated key: check for duplicates first. Hybrid tables enforce their keys.

bands.title: Structure
text: The DDL view comes from GET_DDL. The Structure tab adds, renames and drops columns, sets NOT NULL, comments and the primary key, widens a VARCHAR, and changes a NUMBER’s precision at the same scale.
Changes Snowflake would reject are refused before anything runs: shrinking a VARCHAR, any other type change, and setting a column default to a new value. Clearing a default runs.

moveData: Import {importFormats} files, and export a table or a result to your Mac as {exportFormats}. Server-Side Export, under File > Server-Side Export…, runs COPY INTO a stage with your privileges and writes gzipped CSV, Parquet or JSON that never passes through your Mac.

faq.question: Why does the sidebar show tables but no columns?
faq.answer: Column details come from INFORMATION_SCHEMA, which needs a running warehouse: set Warehouse on the connection or in Session Context. A database whose objects do not appear at all needs USAGE granted to the connecting role.

faq.question: Why do TIMESTAMP_LTZ values show in UTC?
faq.answer: TablePro reads them as a UTC time, marked Z, rather than converting them to the session’s TIMEZONE.

faq.question: Key pair sign-in says the JWT token is invalid. What should I check?
faq.answer: The token carries your account locator and a timestamp. Check the account identifier and the Mac’s clock, then confirm the public key is registered with ALTER USER … SET RSA_PUBLIC_KEY.
